item: Merrow Kline LLP - VH-401 Patient Data Breach Notification Review
driver: All 70 hours billed by a partner at $890/hr with no associate or paralegal support, unlike VH-402 (the firm's other Data Privacy matter) which used only associate/paralegal time. Looks like overstaffing on notification-logistics work rather than a matter requiring senior judgment throughout.
recommendation: Request a role breakdown of the 70 partner hours; require a minimum associate-hour allocation on future breach-response engagements.

item: Osei Bramwell Fitch - VH-404 Wrongful Termination Defense
driver: Partner hours (48, across two billed blocks) slightly exceed associate hours (45) on this litigation defense matter, a heavier senior/junior ratio than document-intensive defense work typically needs.
recommendation: Request an itemized description of the two partner time blocks (30h, 18h); set staffing-ratio expectations for discovery-heavy phases in the next engagement letter.

item: Corrigan Vance LLP (VH-407) vs. Merrow Kline LLP (VH-408) - Regulatory Compliance
driver: Two Regulatory Compliance matters with similar total hours (28 vs 30) were staffed oppositely: VH-407 partner-heavy (20 partner / 8 associate), VH-408 associate-heavy (24 associate / 6 partner). The partner-heavy approach cost more on fewer hours and drove a larger overrun.
recommendation: Set a shared staffing benchmark for regulatory/compliance review and apply it across firms handling this matter type.

item: Corrigan Vance LLP - VH-405 and VH-406 (Commercial Contracts)
driver: Both matters used a consistent associate + paralegal staffing model with no partner time, and both landed under budget. No staffing outlier.
recommendation: No change needed; use as the reference model for other matter types.

item: VH-401 Patient Data Breach Notification Review - Merrow Kline LLP
driver: Billed $62,300 vs $28,000 estimate, +122% ($34,300 over), the largest overrun in the dataset by dollars and percentage, driven by partner-only staffing.
recommendation: Escalate now if the matter is open; request a revised estimate for remaining work.

item: VH-404 Wrongful Termination Defense - Osei Bramwell Fitch
driver: Billed $63,150 vs $45,000 estimate, +40% ($18,150 over), consistent with the partner-heavy staffing mix.
recommendation: Confirm remaining scope and request a revised estimate plus staffing plan.

item: VH-407 State Licensing Compliance Review - Corrigan Vance LLP
driver: Billed $21,120 vs $18,000 estimate, +17% ($3,120 over), tied to partner-heavy staffing relative to its Regulatory Compliance peer.
recommendation: Discuss whether future licensing-review matters can run associate-led, consistent with VH-408's approach.

item: VH-408 HIPAA Risk Assessment - Merrow Kline LLP
driver: Billed $17,220 vs $16,000 estimate, a modest +7.6% overrun ($1,220), consistent with efficient associate-led staffing.
recommendation: No action needed beyond routine monitoring.

item: VH-403, VH-402, VH-405, VH-406 - consistent underruns
driver: Four matters across three matter types landed 9.6-21% under estimate, a consistent modest pattern suggesting reasonably (or slightly conservatively) set estimates rather than a scoping problem.
recommendation: No action now; if underruns persist next quarter, consider tightening estimates for these matter types.

item: Firm-to-matter-type assignment across all three firms
driver: Each firm handles a coherent bucket of matter types (Merrow Kline: Data Privacy + HIPAA compliance; Osei Bramwell Fitch: Employment + Litigation; Corrigan Vance: Commercial Contracts + licensing compliance) with rates that properly step down by role within each firm. Looks intentional, not inertia-driven.

item: Regulatory Compliance split across two firms with no shared staffing approach
driver: Regulatory Compliance matters go to two different firms with no apparent coordination on staffing approach, likely the root cause of the VH-407/VH-408 staffing-mix inconsistency. Looks like an intake/process gap, not a firm doing something wrong.
recommendation: Specify the expected staffing model in intake instructions for Regulatory Compliance matters regardless of which firm receives the work.
